sentences.text: Parents of deceased Shivaraj Kumar filed application under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.50 Lakhs from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529, asserting that on 14.09.2020 at about 5.30 p.m., when Shivaraj Kumar riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-W-3839 from Bengaluru towards Koramangala, near Kote cross, Service Road, Chikkajala, Bengaluru-Bellary road, driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Shivaraj Kumar.

Immediately after the accident, Shivaraj Kumar has been shifted to Shushruta Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid has been provided, then admitted to Columbia Asia Hospital, wherein treated as an inpatient from 14.09.2020 to 21.09.2020.

In view of the injuries suffered in the accident, in spite of better treatment, Shivaraj Kumar expired in the residence on 07.10.2020.
2.

As on the date of accident, Shivaraj Kumar being aged about 33 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/-
p.m., by working as an Associate Admission Consultant in RVSS Institute of Educational Research &
Charitable Trust, Mahalakshmipuram, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Regarding accident, Chikkajala Traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.122/2020 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC and Sec.134(A&B),187 of IMV Act.

3. In response to the notice, respondents No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective advocates, filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode and consequence of the injuries suffered by Shivaraj Kumar.

In the written statement, the respondent No.2/insurance company specifically asserted that due to the negligent riding of the motorcycle by Shivaraj Kumar under intoxication, the accident taken place and death of Shivaraj Kumar is not the consequence of the injuries might have been suffered in the accident.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 16.10.2021 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-MV-1529 by its driver dashed to the deceased Sri.Shivaraj Kumar who was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-W-3839 and he succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 14.09.2020?
2.
Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of deceased himself ?

5. On 08.12.2021, 04.07.2022 petitioner No.1/ Byregowda @ Byranna deposed as PW.1 and produced 15 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.15.

On 17.01.2023, 15.02.2023,
03.03.2023 Respondent No.1/owner/driver of the car deposed as RW.1 and produced 15 documents at Exs.R.1 to R.14 & R.14(a).
On 09.06.2023, Officer of respondent No.2/insurance company deposed as RW.2 and produced 3 documents at Exs.R.15 to R.17.

On 14.03.2024, 12.08.2024, the respondent No.2/insurance company produced the evidence of Medical Record Technician of Shushruta Hospital, Bengaluru and Dr.Ramesh Reddy as RW.3 & 4 and get produced 5 documents at Exs.R.18 to R.22.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf both the parties and perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of the material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue Nos.1 & 2 ...

Due to the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing No.KA43-W-3839 by Shivaraj Kumar under intoxication and negligent use of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 by the respondent No.1 at the ratio of 50 : 50, accident taken place resulting in injuries to Shivaraj Kumar and in view of the injuries suffered in the accident, on 07.10.2020 Shivaraj Kumar expired.
Issue No.3 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive a sum of Rs.12,19,713/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.4 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issue Nos.1 & 2 :- In the lengthy argument learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner by analysing the evidence available in the file submitted that due to the negligent use of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 by the respondent No.1, accident taken place resulting in the injuries to Shivaraj Kumar, which resulted in his death.

9. In the lengthy argument learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1 by analysing the evidence available in the file submitted that the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-W-3839 under intoxication by Shivaraj Kumar, was the reason for the accident, by relying on the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2021)7 SCC 704 (DB) (Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pearl Beverages Ltd).

In the light of the submissions made on behalf of the petitioners and respondent No.1 and in the light of the Judgment cited on behalf of respondent No.1, I have appreciated the evidence available in the file.
11.

In the evidence affidavit, PW.1/Byregowda stated that on 14.09.2020 at 5.30pm,
when Shivaraj Kumar riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-W-3839 from Bengaluru towards Koramangala village, Devanahalli Taluk, on Bengaluru-Bellary service road, near Kote Cross, Chikkajala, driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 negligently drove the same, dashed the same to the motorcycle,
thereby caused accident, caused injuries to Shivaraj Kumar, for which Shivaraj Kumar taken first aid/treatment at Shushruta Hospital and then taken treatment at Columbia Asia Hospital as an inpatient from 14.09.2020 to 21.09.2020, however in spite of better treatment , on 07.10.2020 in the residence Shivaraj Kumar expired.
12.

In the written statement, the respondents No.1 & 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and specifically asserted that riding of the motorcycle by Shivaraj Kumar under intoxication was the reason for the accident and death of Shivaraj Kumar is not the consequence of the injuries might have been suffered in the accident.

13. In the cross-examination PW.1/Byregowda denied the suggestion that at the time of accident, Shivaraj Kumar was under the influence of alcohol, thereby lost control over the two wheeler, dashed to the car.
PW.1 stated that in the accident his son has suffered fractures and injuries to the head.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that as per the medical records, Shivaraj Kumar has not suffered injuries to the head.

In the cross-examination made on behalf of respondent No.1, PW.1 denied the suggestion that accident took place due to the negligence on the part of Shivaraj Kumar who rode the motorcycle under intoxication.
14. In the evidence affidavit RW.1 i.e., respondent No.1 reiterated the same facts as narrated in the written statement regarding reason and mode of the accident.
In the cross-examination RW.1 submitted non-receipt of any summons from the Magistrate Court, in case summons received, his intention to challenge the documents and chargesheet.
RW.1 stated that after the accident, on humanitarian grounds, shifted Shivaraj Kumar to Shushruta hospital and paid a sum of Rs.2,350/- towards first aid.

RW.1 stated that the doctors in the hospital noticed that the deceased was in drunken state and admitted that accident occurred mainly due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the deceased in drunken condition.
In the cross-examination made on behalf of the petitioners, RW.1 admitted that the chargesheet is filed against him by the police.

15. In the evidence affidavit RW.2/Officer of the insurance company reiterated the same facts as narrated in the written statement regarding reason and mode of accident and status of Shivaraj Kumar during the accident (under intoxication).

19.

sentences.text: As referred above, in the evidence RW.4 Dr.Ramesh Reddy stated that on 14.09.2020 he wrote the contents of the original documents pertaining to copy marked at Ex.R.19 and R.20 i.e., original MLC register extract and police intimation.
22. Copy of the sketch of the place of accident reveals that there was distance of 10 ft., between the foot path and place of accident on north-south road.

The evidence on record shows that at 5.30 p.m.,
collision taken place between motorcycle rode by the deceased under intoxication and a car drove by the respondent No.1 on the service road of Bengaluru-Bellary road at a distance of 10 ft., from the foot path.

Hence, I have concluded that due to the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-W- 3839 under intoxication by Shivaraj Kumar and negligent use of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 by the respondent No.1 at the ratio of 50:50, the accident taken place resulting in injuries to Shivaraj Kumar who took treatment at Shushruta Hospital and Columbia Asia Hospital from 14.09.2020 to 21.09.2020, then on 07.10.2020 in the residence, due to septicemia- consequence of multiple injuries expired (succumbed to those injuries).
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 accordingly.

23. Issue Nos.2 & 3 : In the evidence PW.1 stated that as on the date of accident, his son Shivaraj Kumar being aged about 33 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month by working as an Associate Admission Consultant at RVSS Educational Research & Charitable Trust, Mahalakshmipuram,
Bengaluru and used to contribute entire income to the family.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondents No.1 & 2 denied the allegation regarding the occupation and income of the deceased.
24. In the cross-examination PW.1 submitted lack of documents about the occupation and salary of his son.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of Shivaraj Kumar.
In the copy of the Driving Licence marked at Ex.P.13 and Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.14, date of birth/birth year of Shivaraj Kumar are noted as 15.4.1986/1986 respectively.
Medical bills shows that the petitioners No.1 & 2 have spent approximately Rs.2,26,425/- towards treatment of the deceased.

Hence, I have estimated loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased as on the date of accident - 34 years

Notional monthly income of the deceased Shivaraj Kumar as on the date of accident - Rs.14,500/- per month Add:
50% towards loss of future prospects Rs.14,500/- plus 7,250 = 21,750/-
Less : 50% towards personal expenses Rs.21,750/- minus Rs.10,875 = Rs.10,875/-
Multiplier
applied
is - 16 Therefore, loss of dependency = Rs.10,875 x 12 x16 =

. Hence, compensation is assessed at Rs.20,88,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.2,26,425/-
towards treatment, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.80,000/- (
Rs.40,000/- x 2) to the petitioners No.1 & 2 being parents of deceased, towards loss of filial consortium.
Hence, I assessed total compensation at Rs.24,39,425/-.

sentences.text:
In view of my findings on Issue Nos.1 & 2, the petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.12,19,713/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.
27. In the written statement, the respondent No.2/insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 as on the date of accident.
In the reply submitted to the notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act, the respondent No.1/RW.1 noted his driving licence number.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA- 04-MV-1529 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.12,19,713/-
(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Nineteen Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirteen only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 shall deposit the compensation amount within three month from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in Open Court, on this the 12th day of November 2024).

(J.N. SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.

. Hence, compensation is assessed at Rs.20,88,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.2,26,425/-
towards treatment, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.80,000/- (
Rs.40,000/- x 2) to the petitioners No.1 & 2 being parents of deceased, towards loss of filial consortium.
In view of my findings on Issue Nos.1 & 2, the petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.12,19,713/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA- 04-MV-1529 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.12,19,713/-
(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Nineteen Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirteen only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-1529 shall deposit the compensation amount within three month from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
